The 'AI Effect' is the changing perception of what constitutes AI, which is known as the 'AI Effect' [1]. As the perception of AI in society changes, so does its definition [1]. The AI Effect is the situation when a previously labelled AI system is no longer considered to be AI as technology advances [4].

The three basic desirable XAI characteristics are Transparency, Interpretability, and Explainability [1]. Transparency is defined as the ease with which the algorithm and training data used to generate the model can be determined [1]. Interpretability is defined as the understandability of the AI technology by various stakeholders, including the users [1]. Explainability is defined as the ease with which users can determine how the AI-based system comes up with a particular result [1].
AI-based test generation tools reduced the average number of steps needed to cause a failure from around 15,000 steps to around 100 steps [1].

This is called overfitting [4]. It can occur when the model tries to fit to every data point, including those that may be described as noise or outliers [4]. It can also occur when insufficient data is provided in the training dataset [4].

People sometimes accept a machine's suggestion without checking anything else because they are too trusting of these systems, a phenomenon referred to as automation bias [1]. This bias can reduce the quality of decisions made by 5% [1]. The human may fail to consider inputs from other sources, including themselves, when accepting the system's recommendations [1].

When customer behaviour changes over time but the trained model stays the same, the outputs of the model become increasingly less accurate and less useful [1]. This phenomenon is known as concept drift [1].

Graphics processors are usually better than general-purpose processors for machine learning because they are designed to perform massively parallel but relatively simple processing of images, which is common in ML tasks, and they have thousands of cores, making them more efficient for training and running ML models [1]. General-purpose CPUs, in contrast, are less efficient for these tasks because they are designed for complex operations and only provide a few cores [1].

Annotations in a supervised training set can be wrong for several reasons. Random errors may occur when annotators press the wrong button [1]. Systemic errors can happen if labelers receive incorrect instructions or poor training [1]. Deliberate errors might be introduced by malicious annotators [1]. Translation errors can mislabel data when it is converted between languages [1]. Subjective judgments by annotators can lead to conflicting labels [1]. A lack of required domain knowledge can also result in incorrect labeling [1]. Additionally, complex classification tasks can increase the likelihood of errors [1]. The tools used to support data labeling may have defects that lead to incorrect labels [1]. Finally, ML-based labeling approaches are probabilistic and can produce some incorrect labels [1].

The test levels for AI-based systems are: Input Data Testing, ML Model Testing, Component Testing, Component Integration Testing, System Testing, and Acceptance Testing [1]. Component Testing is described as a conventional test level for non-model components [3]. Component Integration Testing ensures system components interact correctly [3]. System Testing ensures the complete system performs as expected [3]. Acceptance Testing is listed as a test level [1].

The documentation of an AI component should contain the following: General information such as identifiers, description, developer details, hardware requirements, license details, version, date, and point of contact [1]. It should also include Design assumptions and technical decisions [1]. For Usage, it should cover primary and secondary use cases, typical users, approach to self-learning, known bias, ethical issues, safety issues, transparency, decision thresholds, platform, and concept drift [1]. The Datasets section should detail features, collection, availability, pre-processing requirements, use, content, labelling, size, privacy, security, bias/fairness, and restrictions/constraints [1]. The Testing section should include the test dataset (description and availability), independence of testing, test results, testing approach for robustness, explainability, concept drift, and portability [1]. Finally, the Training and ML Functional Performance section should cover the ML algorithm, weights, validation dataset, selection of ML functional performance metrics, thresholds for ML functional performance metrics, and actual ML functional performance metrics [1].

Kavram kayması (concept drift), operasyonel ortamın zaman içinde değişmesiyle birlikte, eğitilmiş modelin bu değişikliklere uyum sağlamaması ve sonuçlarının daha az doğru ve kullanışsız hale gelmesi durumudur [1]. Bu durum, özellikle pazarlama kampanyalarının potansiyel müşterilerin davranışını değiştirdiği gibi, kültürel, moral veya toplumsal değişikliklerle (örneğin, COVID-19 pandemisi) ortaya çıkabilir [1]. Sistemlerin kavram kayması riskine karşı düzenli olarak test edilmesi gerekir; bu testler, sistemdeki kavram kayması tespit edilmesini sağlar ve bu durumun hemen müdahale edilmesini sağlar [1]. Testlerin sonucunda, sistem yeniden eğitilir veya sistem kaldırılır [1]. Yeniden eğitme durumunda, güncel eğitim verileriyle birlikte doğrulama, regresyon ve A/B testleri (B-sistem A-sistemden daha iyi performans göstermelidir) uygulanır [1]. Ayrıca, kavram kayması riski, test verilerinin operasyonel veri akışının temsil edici olup olmadığına bağlı olarak da değerlendirilebilir [6].

Veri zehirlenmesi (data poisoning) saldırısı, bir saldırganın eğitim verisini manipüle etmesiyle gerçekleştirilir ve bu, modelin yanlış tahminler vermesine neden olur [1]. Saldırgan, modelin gelecekteki saldırıları kolaylaştırmak için geriye dönük kapılar veya nöron ağları trojanları ekleyebilir, ancak daha çok, eğitim verisini bozulmuş (örneğin, yanlış etiketlenmiş) olarak kullanarak modelin yanlış tahminler vermesini sağlar [1]. Bu saldırılar, belirli durumlarda modelin yanlış sınıflandırmasını tetiklemeyi hedefleyebilir veya genel olarak, örneğin, bir denetim hizmeti saldırısı gibi, sistemdeki tüm verileri etkileyebilir [1]. Bir örnek olarak, Microsoft Tay chatbot’un, Twitter konuşmalarının küçük bir kısmını bozarak gelecekteki konuşmaları bozulmuş hale getirmesi verilmiştir [1]. Ayrıca, spam e-postalarının yanlış olarak "spam değil" olarak raporlanmasını kullanarak spam filtreleme yazılımını bozma, bir veri zehirlenmesi saldırısıdır [1]. Veri zehirlenmesi, yaygın olarak kullanılan ve kamu tarafından kullanılan AI veri setlerinin zehirlenmesi potansiyeliyle ilgili bir endişe kaynağıdır [1].

The 2022 CODATA adjustment took into account all data available up until midnight, December 31, 2022 [1].
The body that recommends the CODATA values of the fundamental constants is the Committee on Data of the International Science Council [2].

The 2022 CODATA recommended value of the Newtonian constant of gravitation is 6.67430(15) × 10⁻¹¹ m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻² [1]. This value is the same as the 2018 value, as stated in the text, because the data used for its determination remained unchanged [1]. The value is presented in Table XXXII on page 44 [1].
The relative standard uncertainty of the vacuum magnetic permeability in the 2022 values is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁰ [1].
Yes, the elementary charge is an exact constant in CODATA 2022, and its value is 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C [1].
The 2022 least-squares adjustment used 133 input data and 79 adjusted constants [1].

The expansion factor applied to the uncertainties of the data that determine the fine-structure constant is 2.5. This is because the data related to the determination of α, which are the six items D1 through D6 in Table XXV, were subject to an expansion factor of 2.5 to reduce inconsistencies [1]. The text on page 52 confirms that this factor of 2.5 is applied to the uncertainties of these specific data items [4]. Furthermore, the text on page 24 states that the recommended value includes an expansion factor of 2.5 on the uncertainties of both the measurement input data and the QED theory of the electron anomaly, which is directly related to the fine-structure constant [3].
The final 2022 least-squares adjustment gave a chi-squared value of 44.2 [1].
The 2022 recommended value of the inverse fine-structure constant is 137.035 999 177(21) [2].

The proton and deuteron radii are known more precisely now because the 2022 adjustment incorporated new and more accurate hydrogen and deuterium spectroscopic data, along with improved muonic atom theory, which contributed to a reduction in the uncertainty of the 2022 recommended value of R∞ [2]. Additionally, the 2022 adjustment included the Lamb-shift data from muonic hydrogen and deuterium, which have smaller uncertainties than the scattering data previously used [4].
